Know Your Neighborhood

Six Neighborhoods, Two Zip Codes —
Which Manhattan Beach Is Right for You?

Manhattan Beach is divided into six distinct residential neighborhoods across zip codes 90266 and 90267. Each has its own character, price range, and buyer profile. Here's everything you need to know.

Sand Section — Beachfront Manhattan Beach

The Sand Section is Manhattan Beach's defining neighborhood — the stretch of streets running west from Highland Avenue down to the Pacific Ocean, anchored by The Strand and the world-famous Manhattan Beach Pier. This is where Southern California's beach lifestyle reaches its most polished, most expensive, and most coveted expression. Properties here range from The Strand's iconic oceanfront homes to walk-street properties just steps from the sand, and the neighborhood's concentration of luxury residential real estate is among the densest in the country.

The housing stock in the Sand Section runs from contemporary multi-story single-family homes to attached townhomes and luxury condominiums, with virtually every property having been substantially renovated or rebuilt in recent years. The Strand itself — the paved beachfront promenade that runs the length of the city — provides one of the most spectacular front-yard experiences in the world, and homes fronting directly onto it trade at prices that reflect this irreplaceable characteristic. Strand properties in Manhattan Beach regularly exceed $10 million, with some trades approaching $25 million for larger lots.

The Sand Section is where buyers come for the ultimate expression of Manhattan Beach luxury. Inventory is extremely limited, qualified buyers are abundant, and well-priced properties move decisively. Every transaction here requires sophisticated jumbo financing — often well into the multi-million dollar range — and having a lender with proven experience in high-value South Bay transactions is not optional.

Tree Section — The Heart of Manhattan Beach

The Tree Section sits between the Sand Section to the west and Highland Avenue to the east, occupying the central residential core of Manhattan Beach. Named for the canopy of mature trees that line its streets — a deliberate choice by early city planners that has paid dividends for a century — the Tree Section is consistently cited as one of the most livable neighborhoods in the entire South Bay. It combines the best of everything: proximity to the beach and downtown, genuine walkability, community character, and homes that represent the full range of Manhattan Beach architectural expression from renovated original cottages to significant new construction.

The Tree Section is also where the Manhattan Beach Greenbelt runs through the neighborhood — a long strip of park and walking path that bisects the area and provides a uniquely urban-pastoral amenity. Homes on or near the Greenbelt carry a premium. The Tree Section's proximity to Downtown Manhattan Beach — the restaurant and retail district centered on Manhattan Beach Boulevard — makes it one of the most walkable addresses in the beach cities.

The Tree Section is where many of Manhattan Beach's most sophisticated buyers ultimately land. It delivers beach proximity and walkability without the uncompromising price premium of The Strand, and its neighborhood character is difficult to replicate anywhere else in the South Bay. Homes here typically range from $2.5 million for a well-maintained original to $5 million or more for significant new construction.

Hill Section — Elevated Views, Elevated Prestige

The Hill Section occupies the elevated terrain just inland from the Sand Section, running north-south along the bluffs that overlook the Pacific Ocean. This geography gives the Hill Section something that most Manhattan Beach neighborhoods lack: elevation. From the Hill Section, many homes command sweeping panoramic views of the Pacific, Palos Verdes Peninsula, and on clear days, Catalina Island. The combination of ocean views, custom-built homes on larger lots, and proximity to both the beach and Downtown Manhattan Beach makes the Hill Section one of the most distinctive residential addresses in the South Bay.

The housing stock in the Hill Section runs larger and more custom than most other Manhattan Beach neighborhoods. Homes here are typically single-family properties on 3,000 to 5,000 square foot lots, often with 3 to 4 bedrooms and 2 to 4 bathrooms, and more than 3,000 square feet of living space. Many have been substantially rebuilt or renovated to maximize their views and reflect contemporary luxury standards.

The Hill Section buyer values views, privacy, and custom architecture. At price points ranging from $3 million to well above $8 million for significant view properties, the Hill Section occupies the upper tier of the Manhattan Beach market. Jumbo financing with experience handling view property appraisals and high-value loan structures is essential.

East Manhattan Beach — Family-Focused & Relatively Accessible

East Manhattan Beach covers all areas east of Sepulveda Boulevard — the main dividing line through the city — and represents the most accessible entry point into Manhattan Beach real estate. Encompassing three distinct sub-neighborhoods (the Mira Costa District, Manhattan Heights/Liberty Village, and Manhattan Village), East Manhattan offers the full benefit of Manhattan Beach Unified School District, proximity to Mira Costa High School, and the community character of Manhattan Beach at price points that are meaningfully below the beachfront neighborhoods to the west.

The Mira Costa District is the most prized part of East Manhattan, with 7,500 square foot lots — larger than virtually anywhere else in the city — that allow for substantial homes with yards. The Mira Costa area has attracted significant renovation and new construction activity as buyers recognize the value of the lot sizes and school district access. Manhattan Heights/Liberty Village offers a mix of original tract homes and updates at a modest entry price for the city. Both neighborhoods are within easy walking distance of Mira Costa High School, Manhattan Beach Middle School, and Polliwog Park.

East Manhattan Beach draws primarily families prioritizing school quality and buyers seeking the maximum square footage for their investment in the Manhattan Beach market. Price points here generally range from $1.5 million for modest originals to $4 million for large, fully renovated Mira Costa properties — still requiring significant jumbo financing but at a meaningful discount to the beachfront sections.

Manhattan Village — Manhattan Beach's Only Gated Community

Manhattan Village is a unique offering within Manhattan Beach — the city's only gated community, featuring 24-hour security, community pools, Magnolia-tree-lined streets, and a self-contained residential environment that is distinctly different from any other neighborhood in the city. Located in East Manhattan Beach adjacent to the Manhattan Village shopping center, the community attracts buyers who prioritize security, community amenities, and a controlled residential environment within the Manhattan Beach school district.

The housing stock within Manhattan Village consists primarily of single-family homes and attached townhomes, with the community's HOA providing maintenance of common areas, the security gates, and the community pools. The Mediterranean and Spanish Colonial architecture of many homes gives the community a consistent aesthetic character. Price points within Manhattan Village are generally more accessible than the beachfront sections but carry a premium over standard East Manhattan for the gated community benefits and amenities.

Manhattan Village attracts buyers who value security and community amenities alongside the Manhattan Beach school district and lifestyle. It is also popular with buyers relocating from gated communities in other cities who want to maintain that lifestyle while accessing the South Bay. HOA fees and the community's condominium-adjacent legal structure mean that financing here requires a lender familiar with gated community and PUD loan structures.

90267 — Downtown Manhattan Beach & Strand Corridor

The 90267 zip code is a smaller, more compact geographic area that covers portions of Downtown Manhattan Beach and the northern Strand corridor. While 90266 is the primary residential zip code for the city, 90267 encompasses some of the most intensely desirable blocks in all of Manhattan Beach — the area immediately surrounding the Pier, the commercial heart of Downtown MB along Manhattan Beach Boulevard, and the northern residential blocks that command some of the city's highest per-square-foot values.

Properties in the 90267 area include high-end condominiums, townhomes, and single-family homes in the most walkable and beach-proximate blocks of the city. For buyers who want to be within literal steps of the Pier, the beach, and the restaurants and boutiques of Downtown Manhattan Beach, the 90267 footprint delivers that address at prices that reflect the premium of being at the absolute center of everything Manhattan Beach offers.

90267 is for the buyer who wants the most urban, most walkable, most beach-proximate version of the Manhattan Beach experience. The trade-off is density — properties here are typically on smaller lots with less yard space than East Manhattan — but the lifestyle compensation is unmatched. All transactions in 90267 require jumbo financing, and familiarity with the specific condominium and high-density residential loan programs is essential.

Complete Buyer's Guide

Everything You Need to Know About Buying a Home in Manhattan Beach CA 90266 & 90267

Manhattan Beach is one of the most consistently coveted residential addresses in the United States. With a 2025 median home price of $3.3 million — a 10% increase over the prior year — and a PropertyShark ranking of #27 among the most expensive zip codes in the nation, 90266 sits in rarified company alongside zip codes in Beverly Hills, Newport Beach, and Northern California's most exclusive enclaves. Buying here is not merely a real estate transaction — it is an entry into one of Southern California's most prestigious and community-driven cities, and it requires preparation, financial sophistication, and a mortgage advisor who genuinely understands what jumbo lending at this price level requires.

Why Manhattan Beach? Why Now?

Manhattan Beach has a combination of attributes that no other community in the South Bay — or arguably in greater Los Angeles — fully replicates. Two miles of pristine beachfront. A world-class public school system anchored by Mira Costa High School, consistently ranked in the top 1-2% of public high schools nationally. A walkable downtown centered on Manhattan Beach Boulevard that delivers independent dining, boutique retail, and community events at a quality level that exceeds what most cities ten times its size can offer. A population of approximately 34,000 that skews toward accomplished professionals, entrepreneurs, athletes, and creative executives who have chosen to invest in the city's community character as much as in their real estate.

Manhattan Beach is also a market that rewards long-term commitment. The 10% price appreciation in 2025 follows a period that saw a 33% run-up between 2020 and 2022, a modest correction in 2023, and a recovery that has pushed the 2025 median back above the prior peak. Homes here have demonstrated the ability to preserve and grow value through multiple economic cycles — a function of the permanent scarcity of beachfront real estate and the stability of demand from a buyer pool that is not dependent on a single employer or industry.

The question is not whether Manhattan Beach is a good investment. It is what it takes to actually buy here — and whether your financing is in place before you find the home you want.

The Six Neighborhoods of Manhattan Beach

Manhattan Beach is small — just 3.88 square miles — but it contains six residential neighborhoods that differ dramatically in character, price, and buyer profile. Understanding these distinctions is the foundation of a successful search.

The Sand Section is the beachfront neighborhood west of Highland Avenue, home to The Strand and the Manhattan Beach Pier. This is the most globally recognized address in the city and among the most expensive coastal real estate in the United States. Strand properties regularly trade between $10 million and $25 million. Off-Strand Sand Section homes and walk-street properties typically range from $3 million for a dated original to $8 million or more for a contemporary build.

The Tree Section occupies the central residential core between the Sand Section and Highland Avenue, defined by its canopy of mature trees and the Manhattan Beach Greenbelt. This is where many long-term Manhattan Beach residents and repeat buyers ultimately settle — close to the beach and Downtown MB, genuinely walkable, and imbued with the neighborhood character that makes Manhattan Beach feel different from other wealthy coastal communities. Homes here typically range from $2.5 million to $5 million.

The Hill Section sits on elevated terrain above the Sand Section, with many homes offering panoramic ocean views. Custom-built on larger lots, the Hill Section delivers the views of coastal living without the beachfront price of The Strand. Prices range from $3 million to well above $8 million for significant view properties.

East Manhattan Beach covers all areas east of Sepulveda Boulevard, encompassing the Mira Costa District, Manhattan Heights/Liberty Village, and Manhattan Village. This is the most family-oriented section of the city, home to Mira Costa High School and Manhattan Beach Middle School. The Mira Costa District's 7,500 square foot lots are among the largest in the city. Price points here range from $1.5 million for original homes in Liberty Village to $4 million for large, fully renovated Mira Costa properties.

Manhattan Village is the city's only gated community, with 24-hour security, community pools, and HOA-maintained common areas. It attracts buyers who want the Manhattan Beach school district and lifestyle with the added benefits of a controlled, amenity-rich residential environment.

The 90267 zip code covers Downtown Manhattan Beach and the immediate Pier district — the most walkable, most urban, most beach-proximate blocks in the entire city. Properties here are typically higher-density than the surrounding residential sections but deliver an address that is at the absolute center of Manhattan Beach life.

Financing in Manhattan Beach — The Jumbo Reality at Scale

Every meaningful purchase in Manhattan Beach requires jumbo financing. With a median price of $3.3 million and an average sale price in 90266 approaching $4 million, the conforming loan limit of $1,209,750 is barely relevant as a discussion point — the vast majority of Manhattan Beach transactions involve loan amounts of $2 million or more, and transactions above $5 million are routine.

At this level, the jumbo financing conversation is more nuanced than it is in markets like Torrance or even Redondo Beach. Here is what Manhattan Beach buyers need to understand about financing at this price point:

  • Super jumbo programs: Loans above $3 million or $5 million fall into "super jumbo" territory with their own underwriting standards, lender pools, and rate considerations. I maintain relationships with lenders who specifically originate at these levels for South Bay properties.
  • Asset-based lending: Many Manhattan Beach buyers are high-net-worth individuals with significant liquid and investment assets but complex income structures — stock compensation, partnership distributions, carried interest, real estate income. Asset depletion and asset-based lending programs can qualify buyers based on the value of verifiable assets rather than traditional income documentation.
  • Down payment at scale: A 20% down payment on a $4 million purchase means $800,000 in down payment alone, plus $90,000 to $120,000 in closing costs. Total cash to close can approach or exceed $1 million. Some super jumbo programs allow 10% down with compensating factors, which changes the cash requirement significantly but affects rate and PMI.
  • Reserve requirements: Super jumbo lenders typically want 18 to 24 months of PITI in verifiable liquid assets post-closing. On a $3 million+ loan, monthly PITI can approach $20,000 — meaning reserve requirements of $360,000 to $480,000 or more.
  • Appraisal complexity: Appraising properties in the $3 million to $10 million range in Manhattan Beach requires experienced local appraisers with access to comparable sales data. I work with appraisers who know the market and can support the value in high-profile transactions.

Self-Employed and Complex Income Buyers in Manhattan Beach

Manhattan Beach has one of the highest concentrations of self-employed professionals, business owners, and executives with complex compensation structures of any residential community in Southern California. Entrepreneurs, entertainment industry executives, technology founders, professional athletes, and real estate investors are all well-represented in the buyer population — and all face the same challenge: their tax returns, after legitimate deductions, often significantly understate the income that actually supports their lifestyle and purchasing power.

The solution is alternative documentation lending. Bank statement programs using 12 or 24 months of business or personal deposits are available in Manhattan Beach at the jumbo level, allowing buyers to establish qualifying income based on actual cash flow rather than AGI. For buyers with substantial investment portfolios, asset depletion programs can convert liquid assets into qualifying income at a standardized rate. For buyers with multiple income streams — base salary, equity compensation, rental income, partnership distributions — I specialize in assembling the complete income picture in a way that maximizes qualifying loan amount.

Mira Costa High School and Manhattan Beach Unified

Manhattan Beach Unified School District is one of the most significant drivers of property values in the city, and Mira Costa High School is its crown jewel. Consistently ranked in the top 1-2% of public high schools nationally, Mira Costa feeds directly into the nation's most selective universities and offers a depth of AP, honors, and extracurricular programming that rivals many private school offerings. For families with school-age children, the ability to access a public school of this quality — at no tuition cost — represents one of the most tangible financial benefits of owning in the Manhattan Beach school district.

Elementary schools in the district — Grand View, Pacific, Meadows, and Pennekamp — are similarly well-regarded, and Manhattan Beach Middle School serves grades 6-8 with a strong academic and athletic program. For families considering the purchase through a school-district lens, understanding which elementary school feeds which neighborhood, and which part of the city offers the most direct path to Mira Costa, is an important part of the neighborhood selection conversation.

How to Win in the Manhattan Beach Market

Despite the high price points, Manhattan Beach is an active and competitive market. With an average of 34 days on market in the 90266 zip code and a market that saw 196 homes sold in a recent 12-month period, well-priced properties in desirable neighborhoods attract multiple qualified buyers quickly. Here is what positions buyers to compete and win:

  • A fully underwritten jumbo or super jumbo pre-approval — verified income, verified assets, verified credit. A pre-approval letter from a recognized South Bay lender carries weight with listing agents who know the market and know which lenders can actually perform at this level.
  • Proof of down payment and reserves — at the $3 to $5 million price level, sellers and their agents want to see evidence that the buyer has the capital to close. A pre-approval that references verified liquid assets reduces seller anxiety about the financing contingency.
  • Speed to close — I can close Manhattan Beach transactions in 21 days when a buyer is properly prepared. Sellers at this price level often have specific timing requirements, and a lender who commits to and delivers a 21-day close is a meaningful differentiator.
  • Understanding of neighborhood-specific financing nuances — walk-street properties, non-warrantable condominiums in 90267, PUD structures in Manhattan Village, and high-value view properties all have specific financing considerations. Knowing these in advance prevents surprises during escrow.
